runs.text: A comparison on accelerometer and radar windows

Today we present the experiment completed after the previous review. We now apply both CNN and LSTM to both sensors. Our main experiment predicts fall versus no fall from randomly mixed four-second windows. We retain leave-one-subject-out evaluation as a supplementary experiment. We will explain the protocol, compare the results and present the next experiments. Sources: 02_Experiments/Current_Phase_Data_Cleaning_and_Baselines/FOUR_MODEL_PROTOCOL.md and results/four_model_comparison/{window,loso}/summary.json.

elements.name: The comparison now separates the effect of th

runs.text: The comparison now separates the effect of the model from the effect of the sensor.

Previously, we had one accelerometer CNN and one radar LSTM. That comparison changed the sensor and architecture together. We have now completed all four sensor-model combinations using shared splits. We also completed a window-based protocol and kept LOSO as a supplementary evaluation. Sixty trained models support these two current protocols: twenty for random windows and forty for LOSO. The earlier grouped-window experiment remains archived. Source: 02_Experiments/Current_Phase_Data_Cleaning_and_Baselines/results/four_model_comparison/window/summary.json and loso/summary.json.

elements.name: We reused the cleaned dataset and its existin

runs.text: We reused the cleaned dataset and its existing fall annotations.

The dataset covers ten subjects and 130 fixed ten-second clips. Cleaning preserves raw files, aligns sensor data on absolute timestamps and handles invalid annotations and radar padding explicitly. There are 99 valid fall events. The processed window dataset contains 99 fall and 297 no-fall windows. The cleaning verifier passed 130 checks with no failures. Other modalities are stored, but this comparison uses only the accelerometer and radar. Sources: 02_Experiments/Current_Phase_Data_Cleaning_and_Baselines/data_processed/dataset_metadata.json, qa_report.json and code/build_clean_dataset.py.

elements.name: 396 test predictions per model after five rou

runs.text: 396 test predictions per model after five rounds

We use StratifiedKFold with five folds, shuffle enabled and random seed 20261117. Only the labels and window row positions enter split selection. Labels remain attached to the matching sensor values. In each round, three folds train, the next fold validates and the current fold tests. This gives approximately sixty percent training, twenty percent validation and twenty percent testing. Every one of the 396 windows contributes exactly one out-of-fold test prediction per model. Overlapping windows may appear across partitions. Source: 02_Experiments/Current_Phase_Data_Cleaning_and_Baselines/results/four_model_comparison/window/splits.json and code/compare_four_models.py.

elements.name: CNN: 3 convolution layers + masked average po

runs.text: CNN: 3 convolution layers + masked average pooling

elements.name: LSTM: 1 recurrent layer with 32 hidden units

runs.text: LSTM: 1 recurrent layer with 32 hidden units

The accelerometer input has 250 time steps and three channels. Radar uses up to 42 time steps with 22 aggregated features, although actual valid lengths range from 26 to 34 frames. The radar mask distinguishes padding from valid observations, including valid empty detections. CNN has three convolution layers with 16, 32 and 64 channels and masked average pooling. LSTM has one layer and 32 hidden units. Both use dropout 0.3 and a two-class output. Sources: 02_Experiments/Current_Phase_Data_Cleaning_and_Baselines/code/compare_four_models.py and data_processed/quida_windows_4s.npz. Parameter counts come from the saved summary.

runs.text: One shared split for a fair comparison of all four models

All four models use Adam with a learning rate of 0.001, weight decay of 0.0001, batch size 32 and up to 45 epochs. We calculate normalisation statistics and class weights from training windows only. We choose the epoch with the minimum unweighted validation cross-entropy. The decision threshold stays at 0.5. Each model and fold uses a fixed initialisation seed, but this is not a multiple-seed stability study. We score accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, F1, balanced accuracy and AUROC. Source: 02_Experiments/Current_Phase_Data_Cleaning_and_Baselines/code/compare_four_models.py.

This table pools the out-of-fold test predictions, not training predictions. Radar CNN gives the highest accuracy and F1 in this run. Accuracy alone is insufficient because three quarters of windows have the no-fall label, so we also report F1, recall and precision. These numbers describe the selected dataset and random window protocol. We have not tested whether the small differences are statistically significant. Source: 02_Experiments/Current_Phase_Data_Cleaning_and_Baselines/results/four_model_comparison/window/summary.json and predictions.csv.

The chart uses the full F1 range from zero to one. Radar CNN reaches 0.9751, accelerometer CNN and radar LSTM both reach 0.9510, and accelerometer LSTM reaches 0.9378. The best-to-lowest F1 gap is approximately 0.0373. With only one initialisation per model and fold, we treat this as an observed ranking rather than a stable architecture advantage. Source: 02_Experiments/Current_Phase_Data_Cleaning_and_Baselines/results/four_model_comparison/window/summary.json.

elements.name: Radar CNN: 1 missed fall and 4 false alarms

runs.text: Radar CNN: 1 missed fall and 4 false alarms

For each model, detected and missed falls add up to 99. Correct no-fall predictions and false alarms add up to 297. Radar CNN detects 98 of 99 falls and produces four false alarms. Accelerometer LSTM also detects 98 falls, but produces twelve false alarms. This shows why recall alone does not identify the best overall classifier. These are counts per selected window, not false alarms per hour in continuous use. Source: 02_Experiments/Current_Phase_Data_Cleaning_and_Baselines/results/four_model_comparison/window/summary.json and predictions.csv.

elements.name: LOSO per round: 8 people train, 1 validates,

runs.text: LOSO per round: 8 people train, 1 validates, 1 tests

Each LOSO round uses eight people for training, one for validation and one for testing. Subject identities do not overlap across these sets. Every window again receives one test prediction. We use the same four model architectures and training settings. The chart compares pooled F1 values. The two protocols train on different quantities of windows, so their differences do not isolate subject generalisation alone. Radar CNN remains highest by pooled F1 in both protocols, but some LOSO scores exceed random-window scores. There is no requirement that one protocol always give a higher score. Source: 02_Experiments/Current_Phase_Data_Cleaning_and_Baselines/results/four_model_comparison/{window,loso}/summary.json.

runs.text: Shared signal can raise test scores.
The window index sets remain disjoint.

The main protocol intentionally ignores person and source-clip grouping. Across the five folds, 282 of the 396 tested windows overlap in time with at least one training window from the same person and source clip. Each tested window appears once in this total. This shared raw signal limits independence, especially for the sampled no-fall windows. We preserve this protocol because it directly answers the current window classification question. LOSO provides a separate subject-isolated view. Dataset size, limited non-fall activity and a single initialisation per fold also limit the conclusions. Sources: 02_Experiments/Current_Phase_Data_Cleaning_and_Baselines/results/four_model_comparison/window/splits.json, FOUR_MODEL_PROTOCOL.md and data_processed/quida_windows_4s.npz.

runs.text: Compare a two-sensor model with the best single-sensor baseline.

These are proposed next steps, not completed experiments. First, rerun fixed folds with multiple initialisation seeds and report mean and standard deviation. Second, inspect the missed-fall and false-alarm waveforms and review their annotations. Third, compare the current protocol with non-overlapping windows and harder no-fall activities if those are available, while keeping random-window results as the main reference. Fourth, test accelerometer-radar fusion against the best single-sensor model. Metric learning can follow as a separate extension after the supervised benchmark is stable. No additional activity data or fusion result is claimed here.

runs.text: Completed: 4 model combinations, 396 test windows per model, supplementary LOSO

The completed work includes data validation, window labels, shared random-window splits, all four supervised model combinations and supplementary LOSO. Radar CNN currently leads the random-window results at 98.74 percent accuracy and 0.9751 F1. The main experiment intentionally mixes windows without grouping by identity. Our next milestone is a repeated-seed benchmark with an error review and a clear comparison of window sampling choices. Fusion and later metric learning should build on that stable benchmark. The current results support this experimental comparison, but not a deployment claim. Sources: 02_Experiments/Current_Phase_Data_Cleaning_and_Baselines/results/four_model_comparison/{window,loso}/summary.json and FOUR_MODEL_PROTOCOL.md.
